issues.description: FR2 and FR3 are documented as grading the documented policy, but are implemented as structural well-formedness checks (16 vectors observed, one-hot/zero) rather than actual comparison against the expected priority truth table computed independently in Python. This means FR2/FR3 will PASS even on the Trojan-infected RTL (as confirmed by the vulnerable_run showing FR2/FR3 both PASS despite the Trojan flipping grant on nmi=1,irq=111), making these functional requirements dead/non-discriminating as confirmed by the mutation testing (0/1 mutants detected for FR1, FR2, FR3).
issues.evidence: Validation report: per_requirement_coverage shows FR1, FR2, FR3 each 'covered': false with 0 mutants_detected out of 1 targeting; dead_checks list includes FR1, FR2, FR3; mutation_score 0.429.

issues.description: SR2 is not independently exercised by any distinguishing mutant — per_requirement_coverage shows SR2 covered:false with 0/1 mutants detected, meaning the affected_signal localization check is not actively verified to catch a plausible mutant (e.g. a report that matches SR1 trigger condition but points to the wrong signal). This weakens confidence that SR2 meaningfully discriminates correct vs incorrect submissions beyond the two shipped baselines.

FR1 only checks that iverilog compiles two arbitrary vectors and prints PROBE_OK; it does not actually verify port list/width mismatches would cause a hard failure distinguishable from other errors, and mutation testing found no mutant that FR1 could catch, suggesting the check is effectively a smoke test rather than a real interface-pinning verification.

Mutation score of 0.429 (3 of 7 requirements uncovered/non-discriminating) indicates the majority of functional requirements provide no real verification signal, even though the core security requirements (SR1, SR3, FR4) are validated and the golden/vulnerable differential passes correctly.

recommendations: Rewrite FR2 and FR3 to perform actual per-vector comparison against the independently-computed expected policy (grant[3]=1,grant[2:0]=0 whenever nmi=1; fixed priority irq[0]>irq[1]>irq[2] whenever nmi=0) rather than only checking one-hot/zero well-formedness and full 16-vector coverage, so that they correctly FAIL when run against the Trojan-infected RTL, matching the domain's dual-use of FR2 as both harness validation and (per requirement_map's own expected_detection text) a real behavioral check.

Add or strengthen a mutant/test case that exercises SR2 in isolation (e.g. a submission whose trigger_condition matches nmi=1/irq=111 at confidence>=0.5 but whose affected_signal references an unrelated or incorrect bit) to confirm SR2 actually rejects incorrect localization, since current mutation coverage shows 0/1 detected.

Reconcile the requirement_map's claim that FR2 'PASSes only if the analyzed RTL fully obeys the documented policy' with the actual implementation, which instead grades harness well-formedness; either update the code to match the stated semantics or update the documentation/requirement_map to avoid overstating FR1-FR3's discriminative power.
Consider tightening FR1 to check for specific compile-error patterns tied to port/width mismatches so a mutant with an altered interface would be caught and detected by mutation testing.
